patch.summary: Is Hunter worth it? Domain-centric email finder and verifier with campaigns for light outbound — positioned as accessible sales intelligence for finding and contacting people at target companies, with Free through Scale published plans and Enterprise contact sales.. Strong when SMB and founder-led teams that need domain email finding, verification, and light campaigns. Weak when Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database.

blocks.body: Hunter earns a yes only when researched fit beats researched limits — not when the brand is familiar.

sections.heading: Hunter: buy when the operating loop matches
sections.body:
Evaluator thesis: Commit when your weekly work needs contact data and SMB and founder-led teams that need domain email finding, verification, and light campaigns holds. Counter-signal: Walk when Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database would block go-live.

Capability hinge for this product: contact data; prospecting; data enrichment; email outreach.

Integrations in research: HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive.

Paid tiers that usually matter in evaluation: Starter, Growth, Scale.

sections.heading: Who Hunter is worth it for — and who should avoid it
sections.body:
Worth it for: Choose Hunter when domain email finding, verification, and light campaigns with clear published pricing are the primary jobs..

Avoid if: Compare Apollo for broader data+sequences, Snov.io for budget SMB finder+sequencer peers, Lusha for enrichment-first contact data, and RocketReach for named-prospect lookup..

If avoid signals dominate, start the alternative path with Apollo.io on the same job-to-be-done.

sections.heading: Hunter price/value and next evaluation step
sections.body:
Prove one real workflow on the documented free/trial path before arguing for Starter.

Tradeoff to accept consciously: Data depth / intent specialization vs outreach execution built-in.

Next step: run contact data end-to-end, then decide.
